title: Caselet Data Interpretation
tagline: Year 3 — Data hidden in a paragraph: building the table yourself and then answering from it

introduction.overview: A caselet gives data in sentences instead of a table or chart. The first job is to convert the paragraph into a small table of numbers, filling in everything that can be calculated directly (percentages of a total, remaining parts, ratios). After that, every question is arithmetic on the table. The common errors are applying a percentage to the wrong base and missing a part of the total.
introduction.placementRelevance: Caselets are used in DI sections of company and bank tests because they test careful reading as well as calculation.
introduction.realWorldContext: Summarising a business situation described in a report or email into numbers is the same skill.

learningObjectives: Extract numbers and relationships from a paragraph
Apply percentages to the correct base
Check that parts add up to the total

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Part = percentage × base ÷ 100. Remaining = total − known parts. A ratio a : b splits a total into a/(a + b) and b/(a + b).

coreDefinitions: Caselet: a paragraph that contains data.
Base: the quantity a percentage is taken of.
Remaining part: total minus the parts already given.
Derived value: a number you calculate from the given data.
Consistency check: the parts must add up to the total.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A caselet is a table in disguise. Draw the table, fill every cell you can, and the questions become lookups.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Underline every number and what it refers to. Write a table with one row per category. Fill totals first, then derived columns, then answer.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Percentage of base
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Base is the total or a subgroup.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Profit
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Profit per unit = SP − cost; cost = SP ÷ (1 + p%)

mainNarrative: A college has 800 students in four streams. Arts has 25% of the students, Science 35%, Commerce 30% and Law the rest. The percentages of girls in Arts, Science, Commerce and Law are 60%, 40%, 50% and 30% respectively. The Law share is 100 − 25 − 35 − 30 = 10%, so the streams have 200, 280, 240 and 80 students. Girls are 60% of 200 = 120, 40% of 280 = 112, 50% of 240 = 120 and 30% of 80 = 24. Total girls = 376 and boys = 800 − 376 = 424.
A percentage must be applied to the right base. The percentage of girls in Science applies to the Science students (280), not to the whole college.

A shop sells three items P, Q and R in a month. It sells 120 units of P at ₹50 each with a profit of 25% on cost, 80 units of Q at ₹120 each with a profit of 20% on cost, and 150 units of R at ₹44 each with a profit of 10% on cost. The cost per unit is ₹40 for P (50 ÷ 1.25), ₹100 for Q (120 ÷ 1.2) and ₹40 for R (44 ÷ 1.1). Profits per unit are ₹10, ₹20 and ₹4, so the total profit is 1200 + 1600 + 600 = ₹3,400.

In a survey of 600 people, 45% travel to work by bus and 25% by metro. The rest either use their own vehicle or walk, in the ratio 3 : 2. Bus = 270, metro = 150, remaining 180. Split 3 : 2 gives own vehicle 108 and walking 72.

deepDiveAspects.title: Percentage of a percentage
deepDiveAspects.content: "40% of the 35% in Science" is 0.40 × 0.35 = 14% of the college, not 75%.

deepDiveAspects.title: Profit on cost versus on selling price
deepDiveAspects.content: Profit on cost uses cost as the base: SP = cost × (1 + p%).

solvedExamples.title: Percentage of base
solvedExamples.question: Of 800 students, 35% are in Science and 40% of them are girls. How many girls are in Science?
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Apply the percentage to the right base.
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The base for 40% is the Science group.

solvedExamples.title: Ratio split
solvedExamples.question: Out of 600 people, 45% travel by bus and 25% by metro. The rest use own vehicle or walk in the ratio 3 : 2. How many walk?

solvedExamples.title: Profit
solvedExamples.question: A shop sells 120 units of P at ₹50 with a profit of 25% on cost. What is its total profit on P?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Profit on cost uses cost as the base.

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Compute from the paragraph each time.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Convert the paragraph into a small table, fill the totals and derived columns once, then answer by lookups.

commonMistakes.mistake: Profit on cost vs on SP

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: A part cannot exceed its total.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Write the table with total row and column.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: One caselet carries six or seven questions, so build the table once.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I turn a caselet into a table?
Can I choose the right base?
Can I split a remainder in a ratio?
